stories.title: 'Our parents were crossing the border an hour before the flood hit'
stories.summary: Hundreds of foreign nationals are desperately waiting to hear from loved ones thought to be caught in the deadly flash flood and mudslide along the Nepal-Tibet border. Sisters Shreya and Ashna Ahuja are among those anxiously waiting for some news of their parents, Deepak and Madhu Ahuja, who had travelled from Texas to Mount Kailash on a group pilgrimage. "It's only been one day, but it has felt like much longer," the sisters tell the BBC. "We just love them a lot and want them to come home." One of the siblings spoke to their parents just before the floods struck. More than 1,300 people are missing, including dozens of Americans and Canadians. Nepali authorities say more than 380 people have died. About 90 US citizens may have been impacted by the floods, the State Department said on Thursday, confirming that three Americans had been rescued. The Ahuja sisters have contacted the State Department and US embassies in Delhi, Nepal and China, but they say they have no concrete information on the whereabouts of their parents. The region is a pilgrimage site for Hindus and Buddhists, and visited by tens of thousands of pilgrims each year. Radhika Sharma's parents, Ramesh Sharma, 65 and Neelam Sharma, 64, two US citizens who live in New York City, were also travelling to Mount Kailash in the Kathmandu region when the disaster struck. The pilgrimage was their first trip on their own since retiring last year. "I am just trying to find them, I don't have any answers," Radhika Sharma told the BBC.

stories.title: Nepal: Relief camp shelters grieving families
stories.summary: Around 500 people are sheltering at a monastery-turned-relief camp in northern Kathmandu, where many families are still in shock after losing their homes and loved ones in the devastating Nepal floods. FRANCE 24's Shahzaib Wahlah reports from the camp as rescue teams continue searching for nearly 1,000 missing people, with operations set to continue through the night.

stories.title: Putin to hold nine bilateral meetings on sidelines of SCO Summit — Kremlin aide
stories.summary: Major international events provide a good opportunity for bilateral contacts and bilateral meetings, Yury Ushakov said
article_sentences: President Vladimir Putin plans to hold nine bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit in Bishkek, Russian Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov said on Friday.
"Major international events provide a good opportunity for bilateral contacts and bilateral meetings.
Naturally, we always take advantage of this opportunity.
It will be done this time too," Ushakov told journalists.

stories.title: Reports that US wants big stake in Venezuelan oil and gas spark anger
stories.summary: Critics call move to gain long-term access to country’s massive energy reserves ‘predatory’ and ‘unconstitutional’ Reports that the US is preparing to claim a big stake in Venezuela’s massive energy reserves have sparked an outcry, with critics describing the move as a “predatory” and “unconstitutional”. Several media outlets this week reported that the Trump administration – which abducted Venezuela’s authoritarian president, Nicolás Maduro, in January and has steered the South American country ever since – hopes to secure long-term access to its oil and gasfields.
